cn.t: Critics find Allegiance a well-intentioned but uneven musical about Japanese internment, praising its important subject matter and heartfelt performances while criticizing its generic score and heavy-handed execution.

sg.ra: Longacre's proscenium is narrow (35ft wide, 34'10" high) and the house is shallow, so Row D sits very close without neck-craning; Center Orchestra rows D-L fall inside the mezzanine overhang line (which starts around Row H) but the overhang is shallow enough that top-of-stage cut-off is not reported here, unlike deeper houses.

Longacre is a small-to-mid house (1,077 seats) so 'rear' orchestra is still close by Broadway standards; rows L-N sit behind the mezzanine overhang line (starts ~H) which trims a small slice of upper stage but preserves intimacy and drops the price noticeably versus premium D-K.

Longacre's mezzanine is 'not too high' per SeatPlan - the overhang from the balcony only starts at Row B, so Row A gets a clean head-on elevated view, and unusually generous front-row legroom is a Longacre-specific quirk called out on BroadwayWorld.

Rows D-E sit under the balcony overhang (starts Row B) but Longacre's balcony is small (249 seats, 7 rows) so the overhang depth is modest; sources consistently flag D-E as the honest middle-ground for elevated sightlines before rows F-J start feeling far from the stage.

Longacre's mezzanine rake flattens toward the back per SeatPlan ('the rake may also be slightly too shallow if a taller patron is sitting in front'), and rows F-J are explicitly called out as 'problematic' and 'not the best on account of their considerable distance from the stage' - the small house becomes a disadvantage here since the balcony takes over the better upper-level views.

Longacre-specific quirk: the front balcony rail sits high enough that multiple TripAdvisor reviewers at 5'5" and 5'7" had to lean over the bar the whole show (Macbeth 2022, Swept Away-era 2025), so Row B beats Row A for most patrons - the opposite of the usual 'front row is always best' advice. Also avoid the four structural pillars between rows B and C on the center aisles.

sg.vl: Skip for any show with detail
sg.ra: Longacre's balcony is the oldest-school part of the house - a 1913 Henry B. Herts design with four structural pillars between B-C and a steep rake that gets sound-dead at the back; SeatPlan explicitly warns 'sound quality may be inferior toward the rear' and rows D-G compound distance + pillar risk + tight legroom.
